source_text: Mulier quae conceperit et pepererit masculum immunda septem diebus. Nativitas carnis purificatione indiget. Masculus — sensus fortior.
thought_title: Birth of the stronger sense requires purification
orientation: Origen is commenting on Leviticus 12:2, applying the law about a woman who bears a male child to the soul's birth of a stronger spiritual sense.
pass_a_gloss: Woman who [she] has conceived and [she] has given birth [to] male [child] unclean seven days. Birth of flesh purification [it] needs. Male [child] — sense stronger.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'unclean' for immundus, the ritual and moral state of separation from God.
The noun purificatio is rendered literally as 'purification', matching the ritual context of Leviticus 12.
The noun masculus is rendered as 'male child' to preserve the biological and figurative sense of the stronger offspring.
Origen interprets the male child as the stronger spiritual sense of the soul, so 'sense' is used for sensus and 'stronger' for fortior.

bible_refs.note: Mulier quae conceperit et pepererit masculum immunda septem diebus

pass_b_english: “A woman who has conceived and borne a male child is unclean for seven days” (Leviticus 12:2). The birth of the flesh needs purification. The male child is the stronger sense.

last_rejected.quote: The male child is the stronger sense
last_rejected.why: Latin 'sensus fortior' means 'stronger sense/perception,' not 'the male child is the stronger sense.' The dash indicates allegorical interpretation: male = stronger sense, not that the child himself is sense.
last_rejected.fix: The male stands for the stronger sense.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'Masculus — sensus fortior' equates male child with stronger sense; English correctly renders the allegorical gloss.
